name: koka
why: A functional language with effect types and reference counting that avoids garbage collection, a genuinely different way to think about code.

brief.what_it_is: Koka is a strongly typed functional-style language with effect types and handlers, and its compiler. The compiler takes Koka source files (.kk) and compiles them, by default through generated C code, into runnable programs. The README also mentions JavaScript and WebAssembly backends. Koka tracks the side effects of every function in its type, so pure and effectful code are distinguished. Effect handlers let users build control abstractions such as exceptions, async/await, or probabilistic programs as ordinary libraries.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents Koka as a research language from Daan Leijen and collaborators, built on a small set of well-studied features (first-class functions, a polymorphic type and effect system, algebraic data types, effect handlers) with precise effect typing that makes programs easier to reason about for humans and compilers. The Perceus reference counting work is framed as a way to get fast, garbage-collector-free memory management.
brief.how_it_works: Koka uses evidence passing to compile effect handlers, and Perceus compiler analysis for reference counting, which lets it emit C code without a garbage collector or runtime system. Perceus also does reuse analysis, so functional-style code can update memory in place when possible. The README reports benchmarks against OCaml, GHC, Swift, Java and C++ on allocation-heavy tests, and says these show Koka is competitive, not a precise head-to-head.

brief.install_notes: The README lists binary installers for Windows (x64), macOS (x64 and M1), and Linux (x64). Other platforms must build from source. Source builds need Stack (or GHC plus cabal-install, or a minbuild script), and the repo must be cloned with --recursive. Optional extras: vcpkg (for linking C libraries, auto-detected at ~/vcpkg), Node.js for the JavaScript backend, and emscripten plus wasmtime for the WebAssembly backend. On Windows, set the console codepage with chcp 65001 before building with Stack, and install clang or use Visual Studio's cl. Installing the bundle puts koka in <prefix>/bin, defaulting to /usr/local on Unix and macOS and %LOCALAPPDATA%\koka on Windows. The README does not mention Homebrew packaging.
brief.standout: Few mainstream languages compile to C with no garbage collector while tracking effects in the type system. Perceus reference counting with reuse, which turns functional code into in-place updates, is the distinctive part. Effect handlers as the one general mechanism for exceptions, async and similar features also sets it apart from typical functional languages.
brief.status: Maintained, by the README's own account. It lists the latest release as v3.2.9, dated 2026-09-17, and has a Recent Releases section pointing to whatsnew notes. It also says Koka v3 is still under development. I did not check commit history, so the status rests on the README's release date.
brief.caveats: The README says Koka v3 is a research language 'not quite ready for production use'. Binary installers cover only three platforms. Building from source needs Haskell tooling, and the Windows setup has extra steps. Package management for Koka modules is still on the to-do list, and the async library with libuv integration is not yet ported. The parallel task support is described as very basic. The benchmark numbers are from Koka v2 on a 2020 machine and are dated. The homepage http://koka-lang.org only redirects, and I could not see the destination.
